result:
I tested 9 properties of `eml_parser.parser` and found 2 genuine bugs; the other 7 passed. Both bugs reproduce every time with a short standalone script.

### Bug 1 — `ignore_bad_start=True` corrupts every e-mail (High, Logic)
`decode_email_bytes` has two faults in this path, at `parser.py:229-237`:
- **The guard almost always fires.** `b':' not in eml_file.split(b'\n', 1)` checks whether `b':'` is an item in a list of lines, not whether the first line contains a colon. So the "skip junk" path runs even on valid e-mails.
- **Newlines are dropped.** The loop rebuilds the message with `_eml_file += line`, without putting back the `\n` that `split` removed. All lines get fused into one.

Example: the valid message `From: a@b.com\nTo: c@d.org\nSubject: hi\n\n...` parsed with `ignore_bad_start=True` comes back with subject `''`, `to` as `[]`, and one header `{'from': ['a@b.comTo, <>']}`. Hypothesis found this with no junk lines at all.

Report: `bug_report_eml_parser_parser_2026-10-06_02-02_jybf.md`

### Bug 2 — `email_force_tld=True` affects every other parser (Medium, Logic)
`EmlParser.__init__` (`parser.py:173-174`) replaces the shared module-level `eml_parser.regexes.email_regex`. Once anyone creates a parser with `email_force_tld=True`, every parser in the same process acts as if the option were on, including ones created later with the default `False`. For example, `john@doe` is no longer extracted from bodies, and nothing restores the original regex.

Report: `bug_report_eml_parser_parser_2026-10-06_02-02_3frt.md`

Both reports include the failing test, a repro script and a suggested patch. I didn't apply any fix to the checkout.

### Properties that passed
- No crashes on arbitrary bytes, on random header/body messages, or on 3,000 fuzzed malformed headers (`From`, `To`, `Received`, `Message-ID` and others).
- No crashes on random nested MIME trees with mixed encodings, charsets, filenames and `message/rfc822` parts.
- The body is cut into chunks before URL scanning; this keeps every character of the body and doesn't lose URLs at any position or with any separator.
- Body regexes (URL, `www`, `href`, e-mail, domain, IPv6) scaled linearly on adversarial inputs.

One side observation, not filed: parse time on a very long `To:` header with many addresses grows roughly quadratically (about 0.35s → 4s as the header grows 4×). The time appears to be spent in Python's standard `email` library rather than in `eml_parser`, so I didn't report it.

All test files are in `runs/eml-parser_r4/work/`.
